extracted.intended_audience: students and professors of broadcast journalism; aspiring radio and television journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook-level practical guide covering the fundamentals and contemporary practices of radio and television news production, including new material on multimedia convergence and digital workflows. Intended to teach how to gather, write, produce, edit and present broadcast news across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering news sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the basics of broadcasting the book covers; implies techniques and standards for identifying, sourcing, verifying and cultivating news contacts and material for radio and television reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among the core topics; encompasses approaches to preparing, conducting, and using interviews effectively in broadcast stories (questions, tone, on-camera/mic technique, legal/ethical considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Putting together a programme
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers structuring a broadcast programme — selecting stories, ordering segments, timing, transitions, and producing a coherent bulletin or show for radio/TV audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: News writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized as a basic skill for broadcasting; includes principles of writing for audio and visual media (clarity, concision, conversational tone, script formatting, lead writing, seconds/words constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General reporting techniques for broadcast journalists, including field reporting, gathering facts, verification, observational skills, and adapting copy for radio/television delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers editing as a core production activity — likely including audio and video editing principles, selecting soundbites, pacing, continuity, and technical/ethical considerations in assembling stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working in the studio
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on studio roles, presenter skills, desk operation, camera and sound interaction, running orders, and coordinating studio production for live and recorded segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducting live reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the particular skills and constraints of live reporting — preparing copy, handling interruptions, communication with the studio, timing, and maintaining accuracy under pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia broadcast news / convergent journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: behind the scenes perspectives on multimedia broadcast news, where it is heading, and how you get there
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The edition presents material on convergent journalism and multimedia approaches, indicating standards for integrating audio, video, web and other platforms into coherent news coverage and production workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital workflow and 24/7 reporting adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology is meshing global and local news. Constant interactivity between on-the-scene reporting and nearly instantaneous broadcasting to the world has changed the very nature of how broadcast journalists must think, act, write and report on a 24/7 basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes adapting journalistic practice to digital workflows and continuous news cycles — implying criteria such as speed with accuracy, cross-platform repurposing, social interaction, and real-time verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcasting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as new coverage in this edition; implies standards for audio storytelling tailored to on-demand distribution, including audience engagement, episode structure, and audio production values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among topics; suggests evaluation criteria for combining text, audio, video, graphics and interactive elements to tell broadcast-origin stories across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered as a contemporary phenomenon; implies guidance on using citizen-generated content (verification, ethical considerations, editorial selection, rights and attribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with broadcast terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Glossary of terms used in digital and multimedia broadcasting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book includes a glossary and a list of common terms and phrases (e.g., angle, audio, Autocue, package, running order, shot, sequence), implying a competency criterion of knowing and correctly using industry terminology.
